record.original_question: Fix an integer n ≥ 1. A generalized knot in S^3 is an oriented immersed circle with only double-point self-intersections, such that the two tangent vectors at each double point are distinct. Let I be an ambient-isotopy invariant of generalized knots in S^3 with at least n double points, and suppose that I integrates to an invariant of generalized knots with n−1 double points in the following sense: there exists an invariant I′ of generalized knots with n−1 double points such that I(K) = Σ_{p∈D}(I′(K^+_p) − I′(K^-_p)), where D is the set of double points of K, K^+_p is obtained by resolving the double point p into one crossing, and K^-_p is obtained by resolving the same double point into the opposite crossing. Must I then integrate all the way to an invariant of honest knots?

evidence.quote: A generalized knot in S^3 is an oriented, immersed circle with only double point self intersections, and where the two tangent vectors to each double point are distinct. Now, let I denote and ambient, isotopy invariant of generalized knots in S^3 with at least n double points. Suppose that I integrates to an invariant of generalized knots with

n − 1 double points. Does I then integrate to an invariant of honest knots? Note that an invariant, I, immersed circles with n double points is said to integrate to an invariant of circles with n − 1 double points when there exists and invariant of the latter, I′, with the property that I(K) = Σ_{p∈D}(I′(K^+_p) − I′(K^-_p)). Here, the sum is over the set D of double points of K; and K^+_p and K^-_p are the generalized knots with n−1 double points which are obtained from K as follows: First, view K so that a neighbourhood of p in K looks like and x with both branches oriented to point towards the top of the page. Then, K^+_p is obtained by resolving the cross with the branch/passing over the other branch. Meanwhile, K^-_p is obtained by resolving the double point using the opposite crossing.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the oriented 3-sphere S^3. A generalized knot in S^3 is an oriented immersed circle whose only self-intersections are transverse double points (so at each double point the two tangent vectors are linearly independent). For each integer m ≥ 0, let K_m denote the set of generalized knots with exactly m double points, considered up to ambient isotopy.

Given a generalized knot K ∈ K_m and a double point p of K, choose a small disk neighborhood of p in which the two branches of K appear as an "X" with both strands oriented upward. Define K^+_p ∈ K_{m-1} to be the generalized knot obtained by replacing this crossing by the resolution in which the strand from lower-left to upper-right passes over the strand from lower-right to upper-left, and define K^-_p ∈ K_{m-1} to be the resolution with the opposite over/under choice.

Let n ≥ 1 be a fixed integer. An ambient-isotopy invariant I defined on generalized knots with at least n double points is said to integrate to an invariant of generalized knots with n−1 double points if there exists an invariant I′ on K_{n-1} such that, for every K ∈ K_n with set of double points D,
   I(K) = Σ_{p ∈ D} ( I′(K^+_p) − I′(K^-_p) ).
By iterating, one says that I integrates all the way to an invariant of honest knots (elements of K_0) if there is a chain of invariants on K_{n-1}, K_{n-2}, …, K_0 each integrating the previous one.

Question: Suppose I is an invariant of generalized knots with at least n double points which integrates to some invariant of K_{n-1}. Must I then necessarily integrate all the way down to an invariant of honest knots in K_0?
artifact.status_search_result: General web searches on integration of finite-type/Vassiliev-style invariants of singular knots did not surface a published resolution of this specific iterated-integration question. Related questions on realizing weight systems via the Kontsevich integral are settled over Q, but the precise question of whether one-step integrability forces full integrability to honest knot invariants does not appear to have a documented answer in the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Finite type invariant - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Vassiliev's idea is to study the prolongation of knot invariants to singular knots via skein-type relations at double points.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the singular-knot/integration framework, but no resolution of the specific question is given.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to Vassiliev Knot Invariants (arXiv:1103.5628)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Vassiliev theory including realization of weight systems via the Kontsevich integral over Q.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references discuss integration of weight systems but do not address the iterated-integration implication asked here.
